title: GLP-1 eligibility assessment, version 2
note: English data for the same engine. Option values (v), scores, flags and conditions must stay identical to data/quiz-v2.json; only text changes. ui sets the answer style (scale for ordered options, reveal for an optional step); slider on a number field is [from, to, start]. s on a condition option is its lowercase wording inside a sentence.

steps.title: How old are you?
What is your biological sex?
Are you pregnant, breastfeeding or planning a pregnancy?

flag.text: These medicines are not used during pregnancy.
Their safety during breastfeeding has not been established, so they are not used.

options.t: I plan to get pregnant in the next 2 months

flag.text: Semaglutide is stopped at least 2 months before trying to conceive; starting it now is not appropriate.

steps.title: Do you or a family member have a history of medullary thyroid cancer or MEN 2 syndrome?
steps.subtitle: Medullary cancer is a rare type of thyroid cancer. Simple nodules, an underactive or an overactive thyroid do not count.

options.d: I have a personal or family history

flag.text: A personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or MEN 2 is an absolute contraindication.

options.d: A doctor should check before any decision

flag.text: Your history of medullary thyroid cancer is unclear.
flag.doctor: Ask exactly which type of thyroid cancer runs in the family; calcitonin if needed

steps.title: Have you ever had a serious allergic reaction to medicines in this group?

options.d: Widespread hives, swelling of the face or lips, or trouble breathing

flag.text: A previous serious allergic reaction to these medicines is a contraindication.

options.t: No / I have never used them

steps.title: What are your height, weight and waist size?

fields.name: waist
fields.label: Waist
fields.hint: Place the tape at your navel and read it after a normal breath out.

steps.title: What is your ethnic background?
steps.subtitle: In some groups, health risks start at a lower BMI.

steps.title: How has your weight changed in the last 6 months?

flag.text: Fast weight loss without a reason should be checked before any treatment.
flag.doctor: Investigate the unintended weight loss (thyroid, uncontrolled diabetes and other causes)

steps.title: Which of these conditions do you have?

options.t: Knee or hip pain with joint stiffness

flag.text: Kidney disease: dehydration from vomiting or diarrhoea can harm the kidneys.
flag.doctor: Creatinine and eGFR before starting and after every dose increase

flag.text: These medicines are not approved for type 1 diabetes and carry a risk of low blood sugar.

steps.title: Which of these are true about your sleep?

options.t: Tiredness or sleepiness during the day
Others have seen your breathing stop in your sleep

steps.title: How much does your weight limit your daily activities?

options.d: Short of breath on stairs or tiring early
Long walks or standing are hard
Daily tasks are hard without help

steps.title: Which of these have you had?

flag.text: History of pancreatitis: use with great caution, or not at all.
flag.doctor: Find the cause of the previous pancreatitis; amylase and lipase if there is abdominal pain

options.t: Slow stomach emptying or chronic nausea

flag.text: These medicines slow stomach emptying further and symptoms may get worse.
flag.doctor: Assess how severe the stomach symptoms are

flag.text: Fast weight loss raises the risk of gallstones.
Dehydration from stomach side effects can harm the kidneys.
A fast drop in blood sugar with semaglutide may worsen retinopathy.

options.t: Weight-loss or bowel surgery in the past

flag.text: After weight-loss surgery, the decision about these medicines belongs to the surgical team.
flag.doctor: Coordinate with the surgeon and check micronutrients

options.t: Surgery or endoscopy under anaesthesia in the next 2 months

flag.text: These medicines raise the risk of stomach contents entering the lungs during anaesthesia.
flag.doctor: Agree fasting instructions with the anaesthetist

flag.text: Heavy drinking raises the risk of pancreatitis and low blood sugar.

steps.title: Which of these medicines do you take?

flag.text: With insulin there is a risk of low blood sugar and the dose will probably need lowering.
flag.doctor: Plan to lower the insulin dose and monitor blood sugar

flag.text: These tablets carry a risk of low blood sugar.
Tirzepatide may reduce how well the contraceptive pill works.
flag.doctor: A non-oral or additional method of contraception

flag.text: Using two medicines from this group at the same time is not allowed.
Absorption of sensitive oral medicines may change.
Some medicines raise weight themselves; asking your doctor about alternatives is worthwhile.

steps.title: A few short questions about eating and mood
steps.subtitle: Your answers stay private and are asked only for your safety.

items.t: Do you make yourself sick because you feel uncomfortably full?
Do you worry you have lost control over how much you eat?
Have you lost more than 6 kg in the last 3 months?
Do you believe yourself to be fat when others say you are too thin?
Would you say that food dominates your life?
Over the last 2 weeks, have you had little interest or pleasure in doing things on most days?
Over the last 2 weeks, have you felt down, depressed or hopeless on most days?
Have you recently had thoughts of harming yourself?

steps.title: Have you used a GLP-1 medicine before?

options.t: Yes, I stopped because of side effects

flag.text: Tell your doctor exactly what side effects you had; a slower dose increase often solves the problem.

options.t: Yes, I stopped because of cost or shortage
Yes, I stopped and my weight came back

steps.title: If you have recent test results (last 6 months), enter them
steps.subtitle: This is optional; if you do not have them, skip this step.

steps.title: How many of your main meals include a protein food?
steps.subtitle: Meat, chicken, fish, eggs, dairy or beans and lentils

steps.title: How many times a week do you do strength training (weights or bands)?
Have you followed a regular diet and activity plan for at least 3 months?

options.t: Yes, regularly, but it did not work
options.d: My weight stalled or came back
I want to start properly for the first time

steps.title: Are you ready for weekly injections, possible side effects and regular check-ups?
Could you cover the monthly cost of the medicine for at least a year?
steps.subtitle: Stopping early because of cost is one of the main reasons weight comes back.

steps.title: What is your main goal?

options.t: Lose 10 to 15% of my weight for my health
options.d: Improve blood sugar, blood pressure or fatty liver

options.t: Lose weight gradually by changing habits

flag.text: These medicines are not approved for losing a few kilos for cosmetic reasons.

signs.labDiabetes: blood sugar in the diabetes range
signs.labPrediabetes: blood sugar in the prediabetes range

under12.text: No medicine in this group is approved for weight loss under 12.

teen.text: For teenagers, weight criteria and the choice of medicine belong to a paediatrician or paediatric endocrinologist.

elderly.text: In older adults the risk of dehydration and muscle loss is higher.
elderly.doctor: Assess muscle mass, kidney function and current medicines

self-harm.text: Right now the priority is supporting you, not weight loss. Please talk to someone today: call your local emergency number or a crisis line where you live.

ed-normal-bmi.text: Signs of an eating disorder with a healthy weight; a weight-loss medicine is not suitable for you.

eating-disorder.text: Your answers show signs of an eating disorder.
eating-disorder.doctor: Assessment by a psychologist or psychiatrist before any medicine

depression.text: Your answers show signs of depression.
depression.doctor: Assess mood and follow it during treatment

possible-diabetes.text: Your test result is in the diabetes range, but you have not reported diabetes.
possible-diabetes.doctor: Confirm a diabetes diagnosis with a repeat test

egfr-low.doctor: A kidney specialist’s opinion before starting

osa-suspect.text: Your symptoms fit sleep apnea; a sleep check with a doctor is worthwhile.

borderline.text: Your BMI is below the official threshold, but your waist is large; the decision about medicine is your doctor’s.
borderline.doctor: Assess abdominal fat and metabolic risk

summary.nonDrug: You meet the official criteria for medicine, but you prefer a non-drug approach. That is a reasonable choice, and you can reassess whenever you like.
summary.borderline: Your BMI is {bmi} and you have not reported a related condition, so the official prescribing criteria (BMI 30 or more, or 27 or more with a weight-related condition) are not met.
summary.notIndicated: Your BMI is {bmi} ({cat}), which is not in the range these medicines are approved for.
summary.indicated: Your BMI is {bmi}{signs}, so the official criteria for medical treatment are met. Your readiness score is {readiness} out of 100{tail}
summary.tailPrepare: ; a few preparation steps are needed before starting.

positives.lifestyle: At least 3 months of a regular diet and exercise plan
positives.protein: Protein at all three main meals
positives.access: Able to continue treatment for at least a year
positives.clear: No contraindications or special cautions were found in your answers

R.label: Contraindicated
R.title: These medicines are not safe for you right now
R.subtitle: The reason is listed under “Contraindications”.

steps.title: Read why they are contraindicated
steps.desc: The reason is in the Contraindications card; no dose or brand changes it.

steps.title: Talk to the right doctor
steps.desc: A gynaecologist, endocrinologist or psychiatrist, depending on the reason

steps.title: An eating plan suited to your current situation
steps.desc: Healthy eating with help from a dietitian, without strict dieting

C.label: Non-drug route
C.title: Start without injections
C.subtitle: By the official criteria, medicine is not your first option; a food and exercise route is safer and lasts longer.

steps.title: A modest energy deficit with enough protein
steps.desc: About 300 to 500 kcal below your needs, with protein at every meal

steps.title: 150 minutes of aerobic activity and 2 strength sessions a week
steps.desc: To keep muscle and improve metabolism

steps.title: Check your weight and waist every month
steps.desc: Aim for 0.5 to 1% weight loss a week

steps.title: Reassess after 3 months
steps.desc: If a new condition appears or your weight does not change, take this assessment again

D.label: Prepare before medicine
D.title: Medicine may suit you, but prepare first
D.subtitle: You meet the criteria, but you are not yet fully ready for a long treatment.

steps.title: 4 to 8 weeks of nutritional preparation
steps.desc: Protein at every meal, enough water, fibre added gradually and small meals

steps.title: Start strength training
steps.desc: 2 sessions a week, so you keep muscle before losing weight

steps.title: Baseline blood tests
steps.desc: HbA1c, fasting glucose, lipids, liver enzymes, creatinine, TSH and vitamin D

steps.title: Plan the cost for at least a year
steps.desc: Stopping early makes weight regain likely

steps.title: See a doctor with this report
steps.desc: The final decision about medicine and dose is the doctor’s

E.label: Medicine candidate
E.title: By the criteria, you are a candidate for medical treatment
E.subtitle: The final decision, the choice of medicine and the dose are your doctor’s. Take this report with you.

steps.title: See a doctor with this report and your test results
steps.desc: Bring a list of the medicines you take

steps.title: A nutrition plan alongside the medicine
steps.desc: Protein 1.2 to 1.6 g per kg of body weight, enough water, and managing nausea and constipation

steps.title: Strength training 2 to 3 times a week
steps.desc: The most important way to keep muscle while losing weight quickly

steps.title: Check weight, waist and strength every month
steps.desc: Discuss losing more than 1.5% a week with your clinician

steps.title: A plan for after the medicine
steps.desc: Plan how to keep the result from the very start

doctorOverlay.title: A doctor should see these points before any decision

step.title: Review the cautions with a doctor
step.desc: Take the list “What to tell or ask my doctor” with you

disclaimer: This assessment is educational and an initial screening only. It does not replace an examination, diagnosis, prescription, or the opinion of a physician or clinical nutrition specialist. The choice of medicine, the dose and how to use it are your doctor’s decision, and your eating plan is your clinical dietitian’s.
